entries.description: Classic two-stage CMOS op-amp: differential pair input with current-mirror load (stage 1) driving a common-source PMOS output stage (stage 2), stabilised by a Miller compensation capacitor Cc between the stage-2 output and stage-1 output.
common_issues: right-half-plane zero from Cc forward path
limited slew rate at low Cc current
PSRR degradation from M5 tail mirror
optimization_tips: add nulling resistor in series with Cc to push RHP zero to LHP
increase M5 bias to improve slew
use cascoded mirror for higher gain

entries.description: Single-stage op-amp using folded cascode topology: NMOS input pair folds into PMOS cascode legs and NMOS cascode bias loads, all driving a single high-impedance output node.
common_issues: limited output swing from stacked cascode devices
optimization_tips: minimize cascode device sizes for noise
add gain boosting for higher Av if needed
ensure Vbias overhead margins across PVT

entries.description: Single-stage cascode op-amp where all signal devices stack vertically: input pair, cascode devices, and cascode-loaded current sources in one branch per side.
common_issues: common-mode input range pinned by stack
optimization_tips: use only when output swing budget is small
favoured for low-power and high-frequency designs
consider folded cascode if swing is binding

entries.description: Single NMOS or PMOS transistor with resistive or active load. Inverting voltage gain Av = -gm*Rload.
common_issues: Miller effect at high frequency due to Cgd
optimization_tips: use active current-source load to boost output resistance

entries.description: Matched NMOS or PMOS pair sharing a tail current source. Provides differential gain and common-mode rejection.
common_issues: common-mode range limited by Vov + Vds_sat of tail
optimization_tips: increase tail device length for higher CMRR

entries.description: Push-pull complementary NMOS/PMOS pair biased near cutoff so both devices conduct for small signals, eliminating crossover distortion.
common_issues: crossover distortion if quiescent bias too low
optimization_tips: use Vbe-multiplier or floating Vbias for stable quiescent current

entries.description: Op-amp with parallel NMOS and PMOS input diff pairs, switching active pair based on common-mode level for full Vss-to-Vdd input range.
optimization_tips: use gm balancing technique to flatten gm vs Vcm

entries.description: Op-amp with input chopper modulation and output demodulation to up-convert offset and 1/f noise above the signal band, where it can be filtered out.
optimization_tips: filter chopper artifacts with notch or low-pass

entries.description: Switched-capacitor amplifier that samples its own offset during a calibration phase and subtracts it during signal phase.
optimization_tips: combine with chopping for lower noise floor

entries.description: Amplifier with low-impedance inverting input current sense; gain-bandwidth is largely independent of closed-loop gain due to feedback through a transimpedance node.
common_issues: limited gain accuracy at low Rf
optimization_tips: keep traces short to minimise stray Cf

entries.description: Dynamic latched comparator: differential input pair charges internal nodes during reset, then a positive-feedback latch regenerates the small differential into rail-to-rail output during evaluation.
optimization_tips: add preamp stage for low-input applications
increase tail current for faster regeneration

entries.description: Open-loop high-gain amplifier driving an output gate; continuously evaluates input vs threshold without clocking.
optimization_tips: add Schmitt-trigger hysteresis if input is noisy
consider a latched topology for clocked systems

entries.description: Two-phase comparator: tracks the differential input during one clock phase, then latches the decision during the next.
common_issues: mismatch between track and latch phases
optimization_tips: isolate track stage from latch with a buffer
use bootstrapped switches for low-distortion tracking

entries.description: Comparator with two different switching thresholds (upper and lower) creating a hysteresis band that rejects noise.
common_issues: trade-off between noise immunity and sensitivity
optimization_tips: use Schmitt-trigger structure with positive feedback

entries.description: Two-stage comparator: a low-gain continuous preamp reduces input-referred offset of the latch and isolates kickback.
optimization_tips: pulse-bias the preamp for power savings
match latch loading to both sides

entries.description: Bandgap voltage reference using two bipolar transistors at different current densities to generate PTAT and VBE components that sum to a temperature-stable ~1.25V.
optimization_tips: add start-up circuit (e.g. small leakage path)
trim BJT ratio or op-amp offset
use cascode current mirrors for PSRR

entries.description: Sub-1V bandgap that sums PTAT and CTAT currents (rather than voltages) through a resistor to generate any Vref below the silicon bandgap.
optimization_tips: use poly resistor ladder for matching

entries.description: Bandgap reference with extra correction loop that cancels the second-order temperature curvature of VBE for ultra-flat Vref(T).
optimization_tips: validate over PVT with Monte Carlo

entries.description: Discrete-time bandgap using switched capacitors to generate ratiometric VBE and PTAT terms with very low offset.
Bandgap targeting sub-µA quiescent current using sub-threshold BJTs or MOS-based VTH-extraction; key for IoT and energy-harvesting.
Low-dropout regulator with PMOS pass transistor controlled by an error amplifier; supports low dropout because PMOS is in common-source with Vsg headroom.
common_issues: stability dominated by output cap ESR
optimization_tips: place output cap ESR in stability zone
add buffer between EA and pass-FET gate

entries.description: LDO using NMOS source follower as pass device; low output impedance simplifies compensation but requires a higher gate-drive voltage above Vout.
common_issues: needs charge pump or higher rail for gate drive

entries.description: LDO without external output capacitor; stability provided by internal compensation network. Suited to on-chip integration.
common_issues: transient response sensitive to load step
higher quiescent current needed for fast loop

entries.description: LDO with digital control loop: ADC samples Vout, digital controller adjusts an array of binary-weighted PMOS pass transistors.
optimization_tips: dithering or asynchronous logic to reduce limit cycles
interleave multiple loops for faster response
extend ADC resolution under load steps

entries.description: LDO whose error-amplifier quiescent current scales with load current, improving transient response without continuous high IQ.
common_issues: trade-off between IQ scaling and PSRR
optimization_tips: ensure stability across all load states

entries.description: Odd number of inverters in a ring, naturally oscillating at f = 1/(2*N*td) where td is per-stage delay.
optimization_tips: use differential inverter stages for better PSRR
calibrate via DLL or PLL lock

entries.description: Oscillator using on-chip inductor and capacitor (LC tank) with cross-coupled NMOS or NMOS+PMOS negative-gm pair to sustain oscillation.
common_issues: Q factor degraded by metal losses
optimization_tips: thick top metal for high Q

entries.description: Capacitor charged/discharged through a resistor with a comparator and reset switch sets the oscillation period T ≈ R*C.
common_issues: temperature dependence of R and C
optimization_tips: switch trim bits at temperature steps

entries.description: Pierce-style oscillator using an external quartz crystal as the high-Q resonant element, with on-chip CMOS inverter and load caps.
optimization_tips: use AGC to limit drive level
tune load caps to crystal CL spec

entries.description: Two LC VCOs coupled in quadrature via NMOS coupling devices producing I/Q outputs 90° apart, used in IQ transceivers.
common_issues: coupling factor trade-off between I/Q accuracy and phase noise

entries.description: Comparator at the heart of a SAR ADC: decides MSB-first whether the DAC output is above or below Vin during each bit trial.
optimization_tips: use StrongARM topology for low energy

entries.description: Per-stage block of a pipelined ADC: sample-and-hold, sub-ADC (flash), DAC subtraction, residue amplification.
common_issues: op-amp gain error in residue amplifier

entries.description: Switched-capacitor or continuous-time integrator forming the core of a sigma-delta modulator; output shape determines noise transfer function.
optimization_tips: increase sampling cap to drop kT/C noise
dynamic element matching in feedback DAC

entries.description: Parallel array of 2^N − 1 comparators, each comparing Vin against a tap of a resistor reference ladder, for N-bit conversion in one clock.
optimization_tips: interpolating preamps to halve comparator count

entries.description: Sampling switch whose gate voltage tracks the input plus a fixed offset (via a bootstrapped capacitor) for nearly constant on-resistance across input range.
optimization_tips: use thick-oxide reliability device for switch
match clock edges for low jitter

entries.description: Basic CMOS inverter: PMOS pull-up + NMOS pull-down. Building block of all digital logic.
optimization_tips: size PMOS ~2× NMOS for equal rise/fall
buffer chains use beta ~4 fan-out per stage
use multi-Vt for power vs speed

entries.description: Two-input NAND: series NMOS pair + parallel PMOS pair. Universal logic gate.
optimization_tips: place critical signal on inner input
use NAND chains for fast inverting logic

entries.description: Two-input NOR: series PMOS + parallel NMOS. Slower than NAND2 due to series PMOS resistance.
optimization_tips: avoid critical paths if speed-bound; use NAND-based equivalent
shallow PMOS in low-Vt for high speed

entries.description: Two-input XOR: typical CMOS implementation uses transmission gates or pass-transistor logic; widely used in adders and parity logic.
optimization_tips: use TG-XOR for low transistor count
balance both inputs to reduce skew-induced glitches

entries.description: Master-slave latch storing one bit on the clock edge; basis of pipelined and sequential digital logic.
optimization_tips: use buffer trees to balance clock arrival
set hold-time margin with delay cells

entries.description: Transparent latch: passes input to output when enable is high, holds value when low.
optimization_tips: use only when needed (e.g. pulsed latch designs)
ensure designers know latch timing semantics
avoid in pipelined paths without time-borrowing

entries.description: Selects between two inputs based on a select line; can be built from TGs or AOI gates.
optimization_tips: use AOI-based MUX for higher drive
balance both data inputs for skew

entries.description: Two cascaded inverters providing drive strength multiplication and signal restoration; used in clock trees and fan-out chains.
optimization_tips: use logical-effort sizing for delay-optimal chains

entries.description: Combinational logic with two inputs and two outputs (sum = XOR, carry = AND); building block of full adders.
common_issues: carry-out path is slow without optimisation

entries.description: Three-input adder (A, B, Cin) producing Sum and Cout; basis of ripple-carry and carry-look-ahead adders.
common_issues: carry-chain delay dominates in ripple form
optimization_tips: use CLA or carry-skip for wide adders

entries.description: Data path that must arrive at the destination flop's D input before the launching clock edge (minus setup time) to meet timing.
common_issues: setup slack negative when path delay too long

entries.description: Data must hold stable at the destination flop for a hold time after the clock edge; fast paths violate hold if launch propagates faster than the clock skew.
common_issues: fix at the cost of dynamic power
optimization_tips: insert buffer or delay cells on launch side
use high-Vt cells to slow short paths

entries.description: Adjust per-flop clock arrival times to push slack from tight paths to slack paths, expanding setup/hold margins where most useful.
common_issues: manual skew is hard to maintain

entries.description: STA reports the longest combinational path from any flop output to the next flop input; this is the path that limits clock frequency.
optimization_tips: GNN-based critical-path prediction can pre-screen risky paths

entries.description: Paths constrained to take more than one clock cycle (e.g. between flops in different clock domains or with explicit multicycle constraints).
common_issues: forgotten multicycle constraint inflates effort to no benefit
hold-time still must meet 1-cycle rule unless adjusted
optimization_tips: verify both setup and hold multicycle specs
minimise multicycle use; restructure when possible
